methods.label: Locate the 21st set and sum it
methods.explanation:
First count how many integers appear before the \(21\)st set. The first \(20\) sets contain
\[
1+2+\cdots+20=\frac{20\cdot21}{2}=210
\]
integers. This sum follows by pairing \(1\) with \(20\), \(2\) with \(19\), and so on, giving ten pairs of \(21\).

Thus the \(21\)st set starts at \(211\). It contains \(21\) consecutive integers, so it ends at \(211+20=231\). Their average is the average of the endpoints, because terms equally far from the ends have the same sum. Therefore
\[
S_{21}=21\left(\frac{211+231}{2}\right)
=21\cdot221=\boxed{4641},
\]
choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
methods.levelReason: Counting preceding block sizes and pairing consecutive integers require only elementary arithmetic-sequence reasoning.

candidate.annotationRationale: Arithmetic-sequence sums determine both the block's starting point and its sum. The method derives the needed averaging rule by pairing; recognizing consecutive integers as an arithmetic sequence is supporting knowledge.
